Rimac and Ecoblox develop AI data centre solution

  • 08 Oct 2026
  • General
  • By Lois Giles
    • Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:09
    Instaread

    Rimac Technology and ECOBLOX have signed a Joint Development Agreement to develop a modular data centre solution combining Rimac’s battery and power electronics technology with ECOBLOX’s AI infrastructure and data centre integration capabilities.

    The companies are targeting the growing power requirements of AI and high-performance computing, where energy availability, cooling capacity and suitable deployment space are becoming increasingly important. Their joint Modular Data Center (MDC) is designed around a compact architecture for high-density workloads.

    The solution incorporates Rimac Technology’s UNI battery modules, with a Battery Management System providing real-time monitoring and control. Core telemetry will be fed into ECOBLOX’s Data Center Infrastructure Management platform for centralised visibility, automated alarms and analytics.

    Power conversion, UPS, precision cooling and IT infrastructure are combined within a single modular footprint. The companies are developing the system for AI compute architectures moving towards 400 VDC and 800 VDC, drawing on Rimac Technology’s more than decade of high-voltage engineering experience.

    “Partnering with Rimac Technology allows us to redefine high-density power delivery for the next generation of AI compute,” said Doug Makishima, CEO at ECOBLOX. “By integrating automotive-grade energy storage and power electronics directly into our modular data center architecture, we are removing grid constraints and enabling cloud providers and enterprise customers to deploy scalable, power-resilient AI clusters faster and more efficiently than ever before.”

    The Rimac UNI battery modules were developed to automotive standards and combine high-performance density, compact packaging, built-in safety and advanced thermal management. The technology is now being extended to AI infrastructure alongside its applications across automotive, energy storage, marine, off-highway, commercial and industrial sectors.

    “Our battery and power electronics technologies have been developed and industrialized to meet some of the most demanding requirements in the automotive industry”, said Nurdin Pitarevic, CEO of Rimac Technology. “The same capabilities are increasingly relevant to high-power AI infrastructure, where power density, thermal management, safety and reliability are critical. Together with ECOBLOX, we are applying these technologies to a new high-power application and bringing automotive-grade technology to AI data centers.”

    The completed modular data centre is scheduled for installation at Rimac Campus in November 2026 as a live demonstration and customer engagement platform.
